title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the handwritten 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. The neighbouring pages are handwritten derived-category computations: a faithful exact functor σ with right adjoint ψ, ψσ ≅ id, Rψ and spectral sequences. This page is instead a typescript page, 'p. 81, IX', stamped 399. It matches the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', LNM 288, 1972), p. 399, slipped into the folder.

Content, end of §6. The setting is potential good reduction. Over a finite Galois extension K'/K with group G, the abelian variety has good reduction. G acts on the residue field k' (possibly not faithfully, with invariants k) and on the p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) group Y_{k'} of the special fibre, compatibly with its action on k'.
- Dieudonné theory attaches to Y_{k'} a free W(k')-module M of rank equal to the height of Y_{k'}.
- G acts semilinearly on M. The inertia subgroup Γ ⊂ G (a quotient of the full inertia group I) acts W(k')-linearly.
- Taking traces gives a 'p-adic' trace function on Γ, hence on I. A priori it has values in W(k'); the footnote says in fact in W(k), by Gal(k'/k)-invariance.
- When the action comes from an action on a smooth p-divisible group scheme C' over S' with Y = T_p(C'), it agrees with the ℓ-adic trace functions (ℓ ≠ p), citing [25 bis, th. 7]. Hence it is then integer-valued.
- An analogous construction handles case 4.3 b): a trace on π' for elements g lying over f_q^n with n ≥ 0, linearised as in the proof of 4.3.2.

The purpose is to extend 'independence of ℓ' for the inertia action to ℓ = p, using the Dieudonné module as the p-adic substitute for T_ℓ.

The page then opens §7. It introduces the Raynaud extension G^♮ attached to an abelian variety A_K with semi-stable reduction, and duality of the abelian schemes B, B'. Setup 7.1: S = Spec V, with V noetherian, separated and complete for an ideal m. A is a smooth group scheme over S whose component group A_0/A_0^0 is finite étale over S_0, and A_0^0 is an extension of an abelian scheme (by a torus, continued on the next page).
errors: Footnote: the semilinear G-action gives Tr(σγσ^{-1}) = σ(Tr γ). Gal(k'/k)-invariance of the trace therefore needs the trace to be invariant under conjugation by G, i.e. a class function on Γ for G-conjugation. Calling this 'immédiat' seems to hide that step, unless it comes from comparison with the ℓ-adic case. This is a minor possible gap.
Typo in the typescript: 'da façon' should read 'de façon'.

ideas.what: Dieudonné module of the special-fibre p-divisible group, with the inertia subgroup acting linearly, gives a p-adic trace function on inertia for potentially good reduction
ideas.modern_name: p-adic analogue of the ℓ-adic inertia representation; precursor of Fontaine's D_cris / D_pst and the Weil–Deligne representation at p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX, 1972); developed in general by Fontaine and others
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, end of §6 (LNM 288, p. 399)

ideas.what: Agreement of the p-adic trace with ℓ-adic traces, hence integrality, when the action comes from a p-divisible group scheme C' with Y = T_p(C')
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-independence including ℓ = p for traces of inertia (potentially good/crystalline case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck in SGA 7 IX; general cases later (e.g. Ochiai, Coleman–Iovita)

ideas.what: Raynaud extension G^♮ attached to an abelian variety with semi-stable reduction; duality of B, B'

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX (p. 399 of LNM 288), misfiled among the 1976 handwritten notes. Its content is published and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: 'da façon' is a typo in the original typescript for 'de façon'.
'π^!' is probably π' (pi prime) in the typescript.
Page identification: the stamp '399' is the page number in SGA 7 I (LNM 288). The page belongs to Exposé IX, not to the cote 136 manuscript.
